chapter: Style, the future of jazz and later playing
title: The future of classical music
summary: He expects classical music to endure.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What do you think about the future of classical music?

I think it will always be – classical music will always be okay. It’s part of the world’s history. It’s like, you can’t deny that there was a Rome or all these things that relate to the early history of the world. This music is the thing that puts you there and is reminiscent of those eras. It has a great importance. I don’t think it will die. Some of it, if it’s played too much, might cause people to shun it, but in general, I don’t think it will ever die. It’s too important.
That’s good to hear, for both of those things.

Yeah, it’s too good. Some of it – you get some people who are writing modern writing and doesn’t have the substance that the older things have, but even out of that you’re going to have composers who are going to come along who are going to write really fine music and be appreciated.
